users.title: Users
users.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Leave empty to keep current.

backups.intro: Backup events: pick an instance, credential and the databases to back up; run now or (soon) schedule it.
backups.name: Name
backups.credentialHint: Leave on “Use the instance's” unless you want a different user for this event.
backups.environmentHint: Taken from the instance; must match the credential's.
backups.environmentMismatch: Mismatch: the instance is “{{server}}” and the credential “{{cred}}”. They must be the same environment.
backups.destinationLocalHint: The “Local” method stores to the default local storage (configurable in Settings).
backups.noDatabases: Click “Discover” to list the instance's databases.
backups.excludeTablesHint: Optional. Comma-separated; skipped from the dump (--exclude-table).
backups.excludeSchemasHint: Optional. Check the schemas you do NOT want to back up in each database; everything else, including schemas created later, is backed up (--exclude-schema).
backups.excludeExtensionsHint: Excluding an extension that tables or columns depend on (e.g. postgis, citext, uuid-ossp, hstore) will make the restore fail. Only exclude extensions without objects used by the database, such as pgaudit. Requires pg_dump 17 or later (--exclude-extension).
backups.excludeEventTriggersHint: Their CREATE, ALTER and COMMENT ON EVENT TRIGGER statements are removed from the dump (the RETURNS event_trigger function is kept). Useful to restore with a non-superuser, as on Cloud SQL, where creating event triggers fails with "Must be superuser".
backups.compressHint: If disabled, the dump is saved as plain .sql.
backups.cleanDefinersHint: Removes DEFINER from the dump to restore on Cloud SQL or another server.
backups.pgCompatHint: Strips SET transaction_timeout and \restrict/\unrestrict emitted by pg_dump 17+, to restore on PostgreSQL 16 or older (e.g. Cloud SQL import). Data is not altered.
backups.verboseHint: Adds --verbose to the engine and shows its live output (console) during the run. Useful for diagnostics; produces a lot of output on large databases.
backups.sqlBackupDirHint: SQL Server writes the .bak to this path on the server itself (the SQL service must be able to write there). Not downloaded/uploaded; size/integrity are read from the server.
backups.retentionHint: Automatically deletes old backups. A backup is purged if it exceeds the maximum age OR falls outside the most recent N. Leave a field blank to skip that rule.
backups.retentionInvalid: Retention must be a whole number greater than or equal to 1.
backups.retentionSqlNote: SQL Server: the .bak stays on the instance host; retention does not delete it automatically.
backups.runQueued: Execution created for “{{name}}”. Check it under Executions.
backups.bucketRequired: The gcloud method requires a destination bucket.
backups.methodCloudSqlExportHint: The Cloud SQL instance itself writes a FULL copy-only .bak to the bucket; no database credential is used. The instance's service account needs roles/storage.objectCreator on the bucket.
backups.retentionBucketNote: The app never deletes backups from buckets: retention only applies to local storage. Use the bucket lifecycle rules in GCS to clean it up.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.cronHint: Format: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week (e.g. 0 21 * * *).

servers.title: Instances
servers.name: Name
servers.credentialHint: Pick a credential from the catalog. You can assign it later.
servers.environmentHint: Environments are managed in the Environments module.
servers.cloudSqlSaHint: Allow the instance to write to the destination bucket:
servers.cloudSqlSaveFirst: Save the instance to test the Cloud SQL connection.
servers.connStringHint: Paste the string Atlas gives you (or mongodb://…) and click Apply: it fills in the type, host and options. The password is not stored here: it goes in Credentials.
servers.connUserDetected: Detected user: {{user}}; create or pick a credential with that user.
servers.connPasswordDiscarded: The password in the string was discarded.
servers.connOptionsHint: Optional. Format key=value&key=value. Supported: authSource, replicaSet, readPreference, appName, retryWrites, w, tls, directConnection.
servers.connSrvDefaults: SRV uses TLS and, unless you set readPreference, {{readPreference}} (reads from a secondary to spare the primary).

environments.intro: Catalog of environments to classify instances (used in the backup file name).
environments.name: Name
environments.codeHint: Short code (PRD, UAT, DEV…); used in the backup file name.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.intro: Reusable backup users. Define a credential once and assign it to multiple instances.
credentials.name: Name
credentials.extraHint: Optional. Encrypted JSON (e.g. GCP service account key).
credentials.extraHintKeep: Extra data is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
credentials.extraInvalid: Extra data JSON is not valid.

storage.intro: Storage targets for backups: a local folder or a cloud bucket. Mark one default per type.
storage.name: Name
storage.pathHint: Server folder where dumps are stored. Relative paths resolve from the API.
storage.serviceAccountHint: Paste the GCP service account JSON. Leave empty to keep current.
storage.accountHint: Account from the catalog used to authenticate against the bucket.

cloud.intro: Reusable cloud service accounts (key/credential) to authenticate and operate (upload to buckets, etc.).
cloud.name: Name
cloud.secretHint: Paste the service account JSON that GCP provides. Stored encrypted.
cloud.secretHintEdit: Leave empty to keep the current credential.
cloud.computeDetected: DBKeeper runs on a Compute Engine VM with the service account
cloud.computeScopesWarn: The VM access scopes don't allow: {{missing}}. It will fail even if the account has the IAM roles. Change the VM scopes to cloud-platform (requires stopping it).
cloud.computeAdded: Already in the catalog: you can pick it in Storage and Instances.
cloud.computeAddHint: Adds it to the catalog without a key; it authenticates with the VM identity.
cloud.computeNoKey: VM account (Compute Engine): no key is used, the VM itself provides the identity. Grant permissions to that account through IAM.

settings.title: Settings
settings.appearanceHint: Color palette and mode. Saved to your user and follows you on any device.
settings.storageDefaultsHint: Target used when an event doesn't specify one (local for dumps; bucket for cloud).
settings.ldapSecurityNoneWarn: Unencrypted, every login password travels in plain text over the network. Use it only if the domain controller supports neither StartTLS nor LDAPS.
settings.ldapSearchBaseOptional: Optional: if set, the user's name and email are read at login.
settings.ldapTestHint: Validates a user and password with the saved settings. The password is not stored.
settings.securityHint: Temporarily locks a user or an IP after several failed logins (local and AD users). With AD it also keeps attempts from locking the domain account.
settings.maxAttemptsPerUserHint: Below the AD account lockout threshold, so DBKeeper stops first.
settings.maxAttemptsPerIpHint: Higher than per user: several people may share the same IP.
settings.cloudSqlHeartbeatMinutesHint: How often "Export in progress…" is written to the log while the operation keeps running in GCP. 0 = disabled.
settings.maxConcurrentDumpsHint: How many dumps run at once on this server; the rest wait in the queue. Cloud SQL exports do not count. Two executions never run at once on the same instance.
settings.dumpInactivityMinutesHint: A dump stops only if, during this time, the file does not grow and there is no output. A large dump that keeps progressing is never cut, however long it takes.
settings.dumpMaxHoursHint: Safety net: total cap even if it keeps progressing. For SQL Server (the server writes the .bak) it is the only limit.
settings.cloudSqlExportTimeoutHoursHint: Time following the export live. After that it does not fail: it keeps being checked in the background.
settings.cloudSqlVerifyIntervalMinutesHint: How often exports past the active follow-up are checked.
settings.cloudSqlExportMaxHoursHint: After this time the export is marked failed (it may continue in GCP). Must be at least the active follow-up.
